sources.entry: OTS - One-Time-Secret sharing platform with a symmetric 256bit AES encryption in the browser. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Go

summary.one_liner: OTS is a one-time secret sharing web platform that encrypts secrets with AES-256 in the browser before upload and deletes them on first read.
summary.what_it_does: The browser encrypts the secret with symmetric 256-bit AES before sending it to the server, and the password stays out of the server's hands; the generated URL contains the secret ID and password. The secret is deleted on the first read. Storage backends are in-memory (mem) or Redis, with a configurable key prefix and an optional expiry in seconds. The OTS-CLI tool can create and fetch secrets from the command line or scripts, including file attachments, basic-auth or token-auth headers for protected instances. The README also documents a bash/openssl workflow for encrypting a secret locally before posting it to the API. The frontend supports i18n translations via an i18n.yaml file.
use_cases: share a password with someone one time
send a secret that self-destructs after being read
create one-time links from scripts or the command line
share files through an expiring encrypted link
how_to_run: Download the release or pull the Docker image from ghcr.io/luzifer/ots
Start it and access the server (see ./ots --help for options)
Optionally configure the Redis backend with REDIS_URL and REDIS_KEY
Download OTS-CLI from the Releases section or build it from ./cmd/ots-cli
Run: ots-cli fetch <url> to read the secret
stack: Node.js (frontend build, per local development requirements)
notable: Client-side AES-256 encryption so the server never receives the plaintext secret
Secret is deleted on first read
OTS-CLI supports create/fetch in scripts, with file attachments and custom auth headers
Pluggable storage: in-memory or Redis, with optional expiry
Translations managed through an i18n.yaml file
caveats: In-memory storage is wiped on restart; persistence requires Redis
Detailed customization docs are in the external Wiki rather than the README
The public ots.fyi instance is operated by the author; self-hosting is needed for full control
